steps.text: Sunday's boiled eggs (50/100 g — 1 / 2 whole eggs), peeled and halved.
Dust the cut faces heavily with suya (5/7 g) — ground roasted peanut, chilli, ginger, garlic, stock powder. More than looks sensible.
Dip: peanut butter (16/20 g) loosened with warm water and lemon, mashed together with the avocado (25/35 g) and salt.
Carrot (100 g) cut into batons to scoop with.

why: Suya is mostly ground peanut, so it needs fat and salt around it to open up. Dry on a cold egg it tastes dusty; against the avocado dip it tastes like the thing you get at a roadside stand.
notes: D0-019 (egg count 2 vs 2.5): resolved cleanly per the ruling's own recommended direction — Sunday now boils 5 eggs (not 4), earmarking 3 whole eggs (150 g: 1 her/50 g + 2 him/100 g) for this snack instead of the fractional '1½ eggs' (75 g) the original card asked for. him.egg changes 75→100 g; 2 spare eggs remain, as before. See prep-a.json Sunday op and macro-drift table (him +71 kcal / +4.6 g protein, driven mostly by this fix plus the suya weighing below).

Seasoning weighing: suya spice dusting was previously unweighed. Standard-reference suya_spice added (own-mix: 3 parts ground roasted peanut : 1 part chilli, ginger/garlic/stock powder to taste, per Sunday's jar). A realistic 'heavy dust' on the cut egg faces: her 5 g, him 7 g. Drift +25/+71 kcal combined with the egg fix above — both intentional, explained.
batchTakeG covers only the Sunday-batched components eaten here: eggs (55/107 g) and suya spice (5/7 g, also mixed on Sunday). Carrot, avocado and peanut butter are fresh additions at plate time.

Cross-file id conflict resolved: this file does NOT define its own 'suya_spice' record in _ingredients.A.json. _ingredients.B.json (Week B rewriter, parallel) already publishes a canonical suya_spice record (520 kcal/22 p/41 f/20 c/10 fibre per 100 g, freebie:false) for its own suya uses — very close to this rewriter's independent 505/20/38/31/12 estimate, but not identical, and shipping both under the same id would fail L9. This card's 5/7 g grams are unchanged; they now price against B's published per100g instead. Macro-drift table below uses B's values.
